instruction:
bmesh Boolean Welder

`/home/user/Desktop/parts.blend` contains 12 disjoint mesh objects `Part01..Part12`, each a differently-sized cuboid. The parts are arranged in an overlapping cluster so adjacent boxes share real volume. Weld all 12 into a single manifold mesh object named `Welded` and save the result as `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend`.

## Requirements
1. `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend` exists.
2. The scene contains exactly one mesh object, named `Welded`; none of the 12 original `Part*` objects remain.
3. `Welded.modifiers` is empty — the boolean result must be baked into the mesh, not left as a live modifier stack.
4. `Welded` is closed-manifold: every edge is shared by exactly two faces.
5. `Welded` is a single connected component (BFS over face adjacency yields one group).
6. `Welded`'s face count is in [40, 200].
7. `Welded`'s world-space axis-aligned bounding box matches the AABB of the union of all 12 input parts to within 0.01 BU per axis.

Canonical approach: union the 12 parts with bmesh (`bmesh.ops.boolean_solver`) or by chaining object-level Boolean UNION modifiers and applying them. The final mesh must be baked geometry with a clean modifier stack.
